tickets.title: E-bike storage and delivery worker congestion on 11th Street
tickets.requester: Chris Messb (public speaker); Keith Powers (State Assembly Member); Susan (District Manager)
tickets.summary: Speakers describe more than 100 electric bikes stored 24/7 on and around 11th Street and 1st Avenue, blocking the street and sidewalk, with businesses closing and one speaker saying the bikes 'might pose a fire hazard, if, god forbid, something happens.' Delivery workers have no legal parking or corral space, and the district manager reports that the precinct plans an enforcement action on October 7 that will confiscate unlegally parked bikes, while organizations ask for tagging instead. Action: Coordinate with the 9th Precinct, DOT and sanitation on a safe, humane solution for the bike storage, including a fire-safety review of the stored e-bikes and mid-block sanitation options, before the October 7 enforcement.

tickets.title: Safety at Manhattan Bridge exits after fatal crash
tickets.summary: The transportation committee chair reports that a recent crash and death at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge has heightened concern about the bridge exits, which the community has raised through prior resolutions. A letter was sent to the mayor and DOT restating these concerns and asking for an update on the Canal Street redesign, which has had no update since January. Action: Press DOT and the mayor's office for a response on safety changes at the Manhattan Bridge exits and the overdue Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Close Third Avenue L stop pilot
tickets.summary: A public speaker who created a simulation from MTA trip data argues that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save New Yorkers time, since only about 5% of riders board or leave there and the stop is not a transfer or wheelchair-accessible station. He estimates a net savings of 1,800 hours per day even when walking time is counted as twice as costly. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about piloting the closure of the Third Avenue stop.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark spots in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Board member (unnamed); Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center (park stakeholders)
tickets.summary: Speakers report increased drug use, homeless encampments and needle issues in Seward Park, and say the park has many dark spots that help hide drug activity. The district manager says a police task force has been moved to the park and that outreach providers already work there, and a board member asked whether mobile crisis teams could be expanded to reduce drug use. Action: Ask the 7th Precinct, Parks and DOT to report on drug enforcement, outreach and lighting repairs in Seward Park, and call 311 for any lights that are out.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community market terms
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee met with EDC about the Essex Market RFP, but EDC could not explain how the committee's two resolutions were reflected in it. The committee asked EDC to postpone issuing the RFP so that the terms keep the market community-oriented. Action: Hold the planned follow-up meeting with EDC to clarify the resolutions and ask EDC to postpone issuing the RFP until the terms are settled.

tickets.title: Allen Street liquor license application denial follow-up
tickets.requester: Michelle Cooper Smith (board member); Carlin Chan (public speaker)
tickets.summary: The board voted to recommend denial of an SLA application for 11 Allen Street, a location near the former Time Cafe operator, citing a saturated area, its proximity to an active temple, and past crowd problems at Time Cafe. The committee had earlier proposed a compromise with reduced hours and no DJs, but the full board chose a straight denial. The community board's recommendation does not bind the SLA, so the applicant can still seek approval without stipulations. Action: Ask community members to attend the SLA hearing to support the board's denial, and have staff add context and 311 complaint data to the resolution.

tickets.title: Correct August SLA resolutions for Cozy Cafe and Soft Hours Tea House
tickets.location_raw: Cozy Cafe; Soft Hours Tea House
tickets.summary: A board member noticed that two August SLA resolutions incorrectly recommended denial of a full on-premises license, when the applications were for beer and wine licenses. The item for Soft Hours Tea House was a beer and wine license, and the item for Cozy Cafe needs the same correction. Action: Correct the August resolutions for Cozy Cafe (item 3) and Soft Hours Tea House (item 10) so they recommend denial of a beer and wine license, unless the applicant agrees to the stipulations.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot in the district
tickets.location_raw: Delancey Plaza; Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue
tickets.requester: Mayor's Office (OB); Arnett Scott (Transportation committee chair)
tickets.summary: The city is installing free public restrooms in the district as part of a one-year pilot, with DOT as lead agency and installation expected in mid-October. Two locations in the district are Delancey Plaza and Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue, and the committee has concerns about access rules and emergency calls. Action: Pass a resolution next month setting out the board's position on access, emergency calls and monitoring for the restroom pilot, and send it to DOT.

tickets.title: Vote on district needs and budget priorities in October
tickets.summary: The district manager reports that the board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies. The district manager also notes that the draft housing plan has about 7,000 units, but 75% are market rate, while affordable housing is the board's top need. Action: Hold the October committee and full board votes on the district needs statement and ranked budget priorities, and have committees take positions on housing plans earlier in the process.
